cards.subject: A verdant valley
lines: The old travellers' lore holds this was rich, green country until Ragnaros was summoned into the world under Blackrock three hundred years ago and scorched it.
Same event, same century as the Dark Irons' fall. The wasteland and the Dark Iron are one wound.

cards.subject: Kargath
cards.tag: The hinge of the Horde map
lines: The only Horde outpost in all of Khaz Modan, named for Kargath Bladefist of the Shattered Hand.
Its flight path is the join between the northern and southern Horde networks in the Eastern Kingdoms.
Lose it and the Horde's map here is two disconnected halves.

cards.subject: What the dwarves found out
lines: Ironforge prospectors dug into a titan vault under this desert and found markings describing their own true ancestry. They were made, not born.
They also woke the Stonevault troggs the titans had sealed in there as a failed first draft.
The troggs tunnelled toward Ironforge, hit Gnomeregan on the way, and overran that instead.

cards.subject: The Maker's Terrace
lines: The excavation shelf outside the door was flagged elite in here. It was only downgraded years later.
The Maker is a titan epithet.
The doorway to this zone is named after a god.

cards.subject: Indurium
lines: Indurium Mineral Veins spawn in the Badlands and inside Uldaman. Nowhere else in the world.
Martek the Exiled, the orc smith in the Valley of Fangs, is the reason anybody goes looking.

cards.subject: Martek the Exiled
lines: An exiled orc blacksmith camped in the Valley of Fangs, banished over an axe he forged for Gath'Ilzogg of the Blackrock clan.
His text swears on "Duchess Pamay's honor". No Duchess Pamay appears anywhere else in Warcraft, before or since.
His companions Rigglefuzz and Jazzrik are named once and never accounted for.

cards.subject: Angor Fortress
lines: The Dark Iron base in the west is not raiding for loot. They are running their own excavation of the titan ruins.
Ambassador Infernus holds it, and he answers to Ragnaros.
The zone is two archaeological expeditions racing each other — Ironforge from the north, the Firelord from the west.

cards.subject: Apocryphan's Rest
lines: A dragon skeleton lying in the open desert, big enough to have its own name on the map.
Buzzards nest in the ribcage and they are the only thing living there.
There is no lore anywhere for who or what Apocryphan was. The name explains nothing.

cards.subject: The buried temple
lines: There is a structure half-sunk in the sand out there with snake-head statues on it, and they match the troll temple statuary in the Hinterlands.
No quest, no NPC, no explanation.
A troll ruin in a dwarf-and-titan zone that the game never once mentions.

cards.subject: Theldurin the Lost
lines: A dwarf alone in the southern flats. He was Twilight's Hammer, scorned the cult, and ran.
"Back away! Stay back! I have a pack full of blastpowder and I'm not afraid to use it!"
"Oh my! Oh my! There is a doom approaching. Mark me! A doom!" In here he never gets better.

cards.subject: Cagg, Boff, Kosh, Wurg
lines: All four camps belong to the Dustbelchers, out of Dustbelch Grotto, and they are not scattered at random.
They sit on the caravan road, preying on supply trains bound for Kargath and the Searing Gorge.
Camp Kosh is sitting on the plunder of an abandoned dwarven expedition.

cards.subject: Lotwil Veriatus
lines: A gnome elemental scholar with a sarcastic assistant and a mechanical guard called Servo.
His work on shackles of elemental binding went wrong and summoned something of considerable size.
Removed entirely in 4.0.3a. He simply vanishes out of the world.

cards.subject: Lethlor Ravine
lines: The canyon filling the whole eastern side of the zone, full of black drakes answering to Nefarian. Elite, in here.
There is nothing at the bottom for you.
It is not a place. It is the border, and it is guarded.
